about: Every finding scripts/parity.mjs makes must match a rule here, or the script fails.
Three verdicts now: OURS, PORT, DONE.
SHAPE is gone. It held the pieces where upstream has the same capability by another
structure — the file store, the folder view, the HTTP layer — on the grounds that
nxzai#373 placed them outside its plan. The goal is `main` upstream equal to
`integration`, not upstream merely able to do everything `integration` does, and
those are not the same statement. So they are PORT, in batches P3-37 to P3-40,
each saying in its note that it is offered rather than owed: the maintainer scoped
them out once and may do so again.
OURS is now only what cannot go: our release workflows and packaging, the demo,
our planning documents and release notes, our own tooling, the quick-actions menu
upstream closed in nxzai#333, and the files upstream has that we do not.
Batches are numbered P3-nn, phase 3, in delivery order. The thirty-three of
nxzai#373 were phase 2. P3-01 to P3-04 are sent and waiting on the maintainer.
The first matching rule wins, so the specific ones come first. `match` is a
regular expression unless `exact` is true. There is deliberately no catch-all:
anything new is unclassified, and unclassified is a failure.

residue.note: when a document stops being reported as open. Here it waits for the document server's own release, because closing the frame is not the server letting go and a force-save is still landing; upstream ends it with the session. Each side has a suite that proves its own, so this one is the maintainer's to settle rather than ours to send
